ctx.x: All right. So leading up to the Mariel boatlift, was there a period of a number of years where you started to think I really am unhappy here, I want to pursue this music career but it’s not going to happen here. I mean what was your motivation to come to the States in such a manner that you did?

I always, Monk, since I started using my mind, I’m also I have to say that my dad, who was a huge Fidel Castro fan up to the point that my father fought on Bay of Pigs defending the Cuban regime. In 1965 he broke ties with the revolution because he started seeing that Castro’s promises — that everything was like a lie. He thought that Castro

items.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: my father was in Castro’s eyes because all of the promises that Castro made to the poor Cuban people

ctx.x: I wanted to just follow up on your early life. And you had said your father was a fan of Castro and fought in the Bay of Pigs and embraced the political situation at the time, is that correct?

Yes. Like millions of Cubans, they embraced the Cuban revolution, I mean coming from a poor family so rightfully so my father was in Castro’s eyes because all of the promises that Castro made to the poor Cuban people, talking about equality, inclusion, and so forth and so on. So anyway, yes he did. He fought on Bay of Pigs and then around 1965 he went the opposite way. So he abandoned Castro’s revolution.
What specifically did he get disenchanted with?
